$comment: SSTIM -> HED event-semantic crosswalk (ADR 0025 decision 2). One-way and versioned: SSTIM event types are the source of truth, HED is generated. Temporal scope uses HED definitions: Onset and Offset are scope tags that HED requires to be paired with exactly one Def/ tag, so the session and the delivery are each defined once below and referenced by the events. An event type may also carry a detailTemplate, whose tags are appended when the event record holds the values they need. Validated by hedtools against the pinned schema in `make hed-crosswalk`.
notes: HED annotations are generated from SSTIM event types; they are never primary storage (ADR 0025 decision 2).
These are profile mappings, not concept equivalences. No skos:exactMatch is asserted between an SSTIM event type and a HED tag, per ADR 0025 decision 6.

Version 0.1.0 of this map wrote scope tags bare, as (Experiment-structure, Time-block, Onset). That is invalid HED: a scope tag requires exactly one paired Def/. The tag-existence check passed it because every tag existed; only hedtools caught it. That is the whole argument for decision 7 requiring a real validator.
Where SSTIM distinguishes something HED does not, the difference is recorded in `lossyBecause` rather than forced into a tag.

Version 0.3.0 added detailTemplate. `hed` remains the part determined by the event type alone and is what a reverse lookup matches after detail tags are stripped; the template carries per-event values HED can express and the type cannot. It exists because two lossyBecause statements were false: they told a consumer that the safety boundary values and the engine identities were 'SSTIM-only', when a sstim:SessionEvent could carry nothing but its type and its clock offset. ADR 0025 decision 5's terms fixed the first; the second was an overclaim and is withdrawn.

Version 0.5.0 applies Kay Robbins's 2026-08-25 ruling that a delivery pause is Offset and a resume is Onset, not the HED Pause and Inset tags. Pause now collides with stop and resume with start, so every member of both collision pairs declares the information a HED-only reader cannot recover. Each event entry also records the SSTIM SKOS notation used as the categorical event_id level in generated sidecars; make hed-crosswalk verifies those notations against the ontology.

eventSessionOpen.label: Session opened
eventSessionOpen.rationale: Opens the session scope defined as Sstim-session.

eventSessionComplete.label: Session completed
eventSessionComplete.rationale: Closes the session scope after the intended duration was delivered.
eventSessionComplete.lossyBecause: HED has no tag distinguishing a completed block from an interrupted one; SSTIM keeps that distinction in the event type, and a consumer reading HED alone cannot recover it.

eventSessionInterrupt.label: Session interrupted
eventSessionInterrupt.lossyBecause: Identical HED to eventSessionComplete. HED 8.4.0 has no Incomplete, Abort or Terminate tag, so completion status is SSTIM-only.

eventPlaybackStart.label: Playback started
eventPlaybackStart.rationale: Opens the delivery scope defined as Sstim-delivery.
eventPlaybackStart.lossyBecause: Identical HED to eventPlaybackResume. HED records that delivery opened but not whether this was the first start, a restart after a stop, or a resume after a pause; SSTIM keeps that distinction in the event type.

eventPlaybackStop.label: Playback stopped
eventPlaybackStop.lossyBecause: Identical HED to eventPlaybackPause. HED records that delivery closed but not whether the closure was a full stop or the start of a pause; SSTIM keeps that distinction in the event type.

eventPlaybackPause.label: Playback paused
eventPlaybackPause.rationale: Closes the delivery scope without closing the session scope; elapsed session time continues while delivered time stops.
eventPlaybackPause.lossyBecause: Identical HED to eventPlaybackStop. HED records that delivery closed but not whether the closure was the start of a pause or a full stop; SSTIM keeps that distinction in the event type.

eventPlaybackResume.label: Playback resumed
eventPlaybackResume.rationale: Reopens the delivery scope after a pause while the session scope remains open.
eventPlaybackResume.lossyBecause: Identical HED to eventPlaybackStart. HED records that delivery opened but not whether this was a resume after a pause, the first start, or a restart after a stop; SSTIM keeps that distinction in the event type.

eventSafetyLimitApplied.label: Safety limit applied
eventSafetyLimitApplied.rationale: A delivery parameter was constrained by a safety boundary. Constrained names the constraining; the detail tags name the parameter and the value actually delivered.
eventSafetyLimitApplied.lossyBecause: HED 8.4.0 has no Safety or Threshold tag, so a HED consumer reads that a parameter was constrained but not that the constraint was protective rather than an ordinary adjustment. The parameter kind and the delivered value travel in the detail tags; the requested value stays in sstim:parameterValueBefore. Which named exposure boundary applied is held by neither side — SSTIM has no term for it either, and this sentence used to claim it did. Confirmed upstream on 2026-08-20: @yarikoptic's answer on hed-schemas#416 is that HED carries the factual delivered value and not the protective intent, which belongs with the higher-level description of the paradigm. This loss is deliberate and correct, not a gap to close by asking HED for a Safety or Threshold tag.

eventEngineFallback.label: Engine fallback
eventEngineFallback.rationale: Delivery moved to a different engine implementation; the change is computational rather than sensory. The mapping is unique, so the event type reverses exactly.
eventEngineFallback.note: No lossyBecause. This previously said the engine pair was 'SSTIM-only', which was false: SSTIM has no engine-identity term, so nothing is lost relative to a record that never held it. Naming software engines is an implementation concern and a separate ontology decision, not something to assert here so that a loss statement reads well.

eventObservationCollected.label: Observation collected
eventObservationCollected.rationale: A phase-qualified report was collected from the participant.
eventObservationCollected.lossyBecause: The instrument, its version, the response state and any unwanted-experience structure are SSTIM-only. HED records that a response occurred, not what it asserted.

eventParameterChanged.label: Parameter changed
eventParameterChanged.rationale: A delivery quantity was set to a new value part-way through the session. Experiment-control places it as a control action rather than a stimulus, Modify names the act, and the detail tags carry which parameter and what it became — which is what makes a segmented stimulus recoverable from the events table.
eventParameterChanged.lossyBecause: HED carries the parameter kind and the new value but not the unit, which follows from the kind and the channel in SSTIM, nor the previous value in sstim:parameterValueBefore.

definitions.$comment: HED definitions naming the two temporal scopes SSTIM events open and close. A consumer must supply these to a HED validator alongside the events, which is what the events.json sidecar does.

parameterKinds.$comment: SSTIM parameter kind -> HED Parameter-label value, for the detailTemplates above. This lived in scripts/generate-hed-bundle.py as a PARAM_LABELS dict until 0.4.0, which was the wrong place twice over: it is part of the mapping contract, not of one generator, and nothing checked it still covered the scheme. A kind added to sstim-v:StimulationParameterKindScheme would have gone unmapped until some fixture happened to use it — the same silent-undercoverage failure `events` is checked for.
